notes: The proof incorrectly assumes the tails indexed by n≥1 enumerate all of J and K, ignoring the given index-0 terms. Its finite-subset supremum identity therefore fails. Take V=R, I=J=K=N₀, v₀=1 and all other values zero, j_n=n, and k swapping 0 and 1. With r=1>0, the j-series sums absolutely to 0 while the k-series sums absolutely to 1, disproving the claimed equivalence.
